title: Continuously split translation-difference sequence for nonarchimedean Banach coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and let $V$ be a complete normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], with $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$ and $\|a v\|=|a|_\ell\|v\|$ for $a\in\mathbf Q_\ell$. Put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its inverse-limit topology and $R=C(H,V)$ with the supremum norm. Give $V$ the trivial $H$-action and give $R$ the jointly continuous translation action $(t\cdot f)(x)=f(x+t)$. Define $\Delta:R\to R$ by $\Delta f(x)=f(x+1)-f(x)$. Then
$$0\longrightarrow V\xrightarrow{\mathrm{const}}R\xrightarrow{\Delta}R\longrightarrow0$$
is an exact sequence of abstract $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector spaces with continuous $H$-equivariant linear arrows. Its kernel is exactly the constant functions, whose inverse identification with $V$ is continuous evaluation at $0$. There is a continuous $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear map $T:R\to R$ with $\Delta T=1$ and $\|Tf\|\leq\|f\|$. More precisely, for the Mahler isometry $\mathcal M:R\simeq c_0(\mathbf N,V)$ [lem-sfb-banach-mahler-coordinates], where $c_0$ is the space of sequences tending to zero with supremum norm,
$$\mathcal M(\Delta f)_n=(\mathcal Mf)_{n+1},\qquad
T=\mathcal M^{-1}P\mathcal M,\qquad P(a_0,a_1,\ldots)=(0,a_0,a_1,\ldots).$$
The section $T$ is not required to be $H$-equivariant. The zero space $V=0$ is allowed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower] with the degree-one extension $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and uniformizer $\ell$. Its ring of integers is $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]; it identifies the norm topology with the stated inverse-limit topology and makes $H$ compact Hausdorff. The addition map is continuous: $|(x+t)-(x'+t')|_\ell\leq\max(|x-x'|_\ell,|t-t'|_\ell)$. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-function-space-complete] to $S=H$ and the complete normed space $V$. Thus $R$ is a normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space and its norm topology equals its compact-open topology.

proof.text: For fixed $t$, write $\tau_t f(x)=f(x+t)$. This is continuous in $x$, linear in $f$, and an isometry since $x\mapsto x+t$ is bijective. To check joint continuity without assuming uniform continuity, use [lem-coef-compact-open-currying] with $K=H$: $H$ is locally compact: inside any metric neighborhood of a point choose a closed ball of sufficiently small positive radius; it is a neighborhood and, being closed in compact $H$, is compact. Its evaluation clause with $A=R$ and $g=\mathrm{id}_R$ gives continuous $(f,y)\mapsto f(y)$. Compose with $((t,f),x)\mapsto(f,x+t)$ and apply its transpose clause with $A=H\times R$ to obtain continuous $(t,f)\mapsto\tau_t f$. Step 1 identifies the function-space topology here with the norm topology. Pointwise $\tau_0=1$ and $\tau_s\tau_t=\tau_{s+t}$, so this is the stated action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent analytic expansion of the inherited scalar-cochain route, using the Mathlib Mahler-coordinate theorem.

proof.text: The map $\Delta=\tau_1-1$ is linear and continuous, with $\|\Delta f\|\leq\|f\|$ by the ultrametric inequality pointwise and the supremum. Constants give a linear isometry $\mathrm{const}:V\to R$ (evaluate at $0$ for the lower bound), hence an injection. The map $e_0(f)=f(0)$ is linear and satisfies $\|e_0(f)\|\leq\|f\|$, so it is continuous. Constants are fixed by every $\tau_t$, and $\Delta\tau_t f(x)=f(x+t+1)-f(x+t)=\tau_t\Delta f(x)$ because $H$ is abelian. These are the required equivariance identities.

proof.text: Restrict the scalars of $V$ to $\mathbf Z_\ell$. Completeness and the ultrametric hypothesis are given, and $\|av\|=|a|_\ell\|v\|$ implies the bounded scalar hypothesis of [lem-sfb-banach-mahler-coordinates]. Obtain its linear isometry $\mathcal M$ with $(\mathcal Mf)_n=(\Delta^nf)(0)$. This formula also shows $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linearity: for any $a\in\mathbf Q_\ell$, induction on $n$ in the difference formula gives $\Delta^n(af)=a\Delta^nf$; evaluation gives $\mathcal M(af)=a\mathcal Mf$. Its inverse is then $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear by bijectivity. The same coefficient formula and $\Delta^n(\Delta f)=\Delta^{n+1}f$ give $\mathcal M(\Delta f)_n=(\mathcal Mf)_{n+1}$, including $n=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent analytic expansion of the inherited scalar-cochain route, using the Mathlib Mahler-coordinate theorem.

proof.text: On $c_0(\mathbf N,V)$ define $S(a)_n=a_{n+1}$ and $P(a)_0=0$, $P(a)_{n+1}=a_n$. Both sequences still tend to zero (discarding or adding a single term does not change a tail). Their formulas make them $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear; $\|Sa\|\leq\|a\|$, $\|Pa\|=\|a\|$ and $SPa=a$ hold by taking suprema. Thus $P$ is continuous. Set $T=\mathcal M^{-1}P\mathcal M$. Step 4 and the isometry in [lem-sfb-banach-mahler-coordinates] give continuous $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linearity and $\|Tf\|=\|f\|$. Moreover $\mathcal M\Delta Tf=SP\mathcal Mf=\mathcal Mf$; injectivity of $\mathcal M$ yields $\Delta T=1$. This proves surjectivity and the stated bound without requiring equivariance of $T$.

proof.text: If $\Delta f=0$, step 4 implies $(\mathcal Mf)_{n+1}=0$ for every $n$, while $(\mathcal Mf)_0=f(0)$. The constant function $c=\mathrm{const}(f(0))$ has zeroth coefficient $f(0)$ and all higher coefficients zero: $\Delta c=0$, and iteration keeps the zero function zero. The coefficient formula and injectivity in [lem-sfb-banach-mahler-coordinates] therefore give $f=c$. Conversely every constant is killed by $\Delta$. Consequently $\ker\Delta=\mathrm{im}(\mathrm{const})$, and $e_0$ from step 3 is the continuous inverse of the identification $V\simeq\ker\Delta$. Together with injectivity in step 3 and surjectivity in step 5 this proves the displayed exact sequence and all its claims. Every formula also holds when $V=0$.
